hypotheses.mechanism: Existing G9 record/provenance/effect-reference semantics plus a typed host DB resource adapter can realize bounded explicit transactions without a DB-specific ClayCode core primitive.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: ClayCode needs a first-class core transaction construct to preserve rollback/replay semantics.
hypotheses.falsifier: A required DB semantic cannot be represented or statically checked with generic typed IR plus stdlib/FFI without hidden backend escape hatches.
hypotheses.test: 2000 randomized differential sequences plus separate-process broker execution.

hypotheses.mechanism: Runtime DB capability/handle identity can remain outside semantic and generated-program identity.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Resource instance identity must be embedded in generated code for correct DB access.
hypotheses.falsifier: Changing only the runtime handle changes required generated semantics or deterministic output identity.
hypotheses.test: 10 successful runs with inherited handle numbers 65..74 and unchanged generated code hash.

hypotheses.mechanism: Host-owned transaction scope plus rollback-on-disconnect prevents uncommitted guest effects from becoming durable.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Process-boundary failure makes rollback semantics unrecoverable without a new language primitive.
hypotheses.falsifier: Crash leaves partial durable state or idempotency marker.
hypotheses.test: Forced guest exit 91 after begin+transfer before commit.

hypotheses.mechanism: A WIT-resource/WASI-style backend could provide a cleaner production boundary than inherited raw file descriptors while preserving the same Clay semantic IR.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Component resource mapping adds complexity without improving authority confinement or portability.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched backend differential reveals semantic mismatch, unacceptable overhead, or remaining ambient authority.
hypotheses.test: Future native-vs-WASI resource differential on Ubuntu target.
